messages:
maya: Heads up — saw steady RSS growth on inference-34 during the long-context chat harness. Looks correlated with prefix cache fragmentation when continuous-batching merges heterogeneous seq-lengths.

drew: How big are we talking?

maya: ~3.2GB in KV pages on that process, plus lots of ~4-8KB free holes. Growth is gradual over ~20–30m sessions, not a single spike.

alex: Any evidence it's the merge step (not eviction)?

maya: Yes — profiler shows a lot of small allocs right after batch_merge events. Also head-of-line delays increase when a large request is merged with several small ones. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-16T21:12:03Z] kv_prefix: alloc_page id=0x7f1 size=256KB seq=1143 from_batch=12
[2026-03-16T21:12:04Z] batch_merge: merged=14 seq_lens=[64,64,512,1024,64,2048...] head_delay_ms=42
[2026-03-16T21:12:04Z] kv_prefix: alloc_page id=0x7f6 size=128KB seq=1144
```

sanju: That matches what I saw in canary — when a large seq enters a mixed batch it forces more page allocations and leaves tiny gaps when later evicted. LRU keeps leaving holes -> fragmentation.

liam: Two quick ideas: 1) split large out-of-line requests into their own batch if predicted_pages > threshold, 2) when merging score by predicted page footprint and avoid merging small+huge.

maya: Tried a simple scoring patch (predicted_pages = ceil(len/kv_page_tokens)). Sort descending, don't mix >8 pages with <2 pages. Quick numbers: tail p95 latency -18%, p99 -9%, throughput down ~6% on canary.

drew: Interesting tradeoff. Any memory improvement?

maya: Yes, peak RSS down by ~1.1GB on that run. Fragmentation_ratio (free_holes_bytes / total_allocated) dropped from ~0.28 to 0.12.

alex: Good. But we should avoid regressing throughput for steady-state RPS. Maybe dynamic rules: allow mixing only under low load, otherwise separate.

sanju: Also think we need a cheap compaction step: background coalescer that merges adjacent free segments during idle periods. That would reclaim holes without changing merge heuristics.

liam: And check allocator: if we use mmap-backed slab we can unmap contiguous free ranges, returning memory to OS, reducing RSS growth. But careful about remapping overhead.

maya: Added extra instrumentation: per-batch predicted_pages, actual_pages, fragmentation_ratio sampled per-minute. Saved traces to s3://redwood/perf/kv/prefix/1769991234.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rolled: prefix-cache-batch-scoring v0.1 -> cluster=inference-34 at 2026-03-16T21:43:21Z :rocket:

drew: Can you share flamegraphs and a short perf diff?

maya: Uploaded CPU+malloc flamegraphs and a diff. Short summary: peak alloc hotspots move from on-alloc path (alloc_page) -> some extra CPU in batch scoring. Overall CPU increase ~3%.

sanju: Next actions I propose:
- land scoring with runtime toggle and autoscale threshold (low-load merge allowed)
- implement background free-segment coalescer
- experiment with mmap slab for remap/unmap
- add unit/integration test for head-of-line scenario (small+huge merged)

alex: +1. Also add a metric for "merge_homogeneity" = variance(predicted_pages in batch) so we can alert if it drifts.

maya: I'll open an RFC + perf doc with numbers and plan. Schedule 30m sync tomorrow to decide rollout. :eyes:

liam: ack. Thanks for the investigation and numbers.

maya: thanks all.
